rungs.stem: In the Ulster Cycle of Irish myth, the hero Cu Chulainn carries one signature weapon that Queen Medb's warriors dread above every sword he owns -- a spear given to him by his teacher on the Isle of Shadow, and the weapon he saves for the fights he is losing. What is the name of Cu Chulainn's signature spear?
choices: the Gae Bolg
Gungnir
Areadbhar
Gae Assail
rungs.context: Gungnir is Odin's spear (Norse); Areadbhar is Lugh's spear in later Tuatha De Danann lists; the Gae Assail is another spear-name in the same Tuatha tradition. The Gae Bolg is Cu Chulainn's alone. Wikipedia: Gae Bulg.

rungs.stem: Before he could carry the Gae Bolg, Cu Chulainn spent years on the Isle of Shadow (Alba) being trained in every warrior's feat by a female fighting-master who tutored heroes from across the Irish world. Who trained him and gave him the spear?
choices: Scathach
the Morrigan
Queen Medb
Deirdre of the Sorrows
rungs.context: Scathach ('the Shadowy One') ran a school for heroes on Alba; Cu Chulainn and his foster-brother Ferdiad both studied with her, but Scathach taught the Gae Bolg feat to Cu Chulainn alone. Wikipedia: Gae Bulg, Ferdiad.

rungs.stem: The Gae Bolg is not thrown from the hand like an ordinary spear. Scathach's rule is strict: the caster must stand in the current of a ford, and the charioteer floats the shaft down the stream on the water so the warrior can catch it -- not with his hand, but with a specific part of his body. From what part of the body is the Gae Bolg cast?
choices: from between the toes of the foot
from the shoulder in an underhand hurl
from the crook of the elbow
from the mouth as a warcry-launch
rungs.answer: from between the toes of the foot
rungs.context: The Gae Bolg is caught between the toes as it floats past and kicked up at the enemy -- a technique some scholars suspect began as spear-fishing. Wikipedia: Gae Bulg.

rungs.stem: The horror of the Gae Bolg is not the throw. It is what the spear does the moment its tip breaks the enemy's skin. The point enters like an ordinary javelin, one small wound -- and then, inside the body, it changes. What does the Gae Bolg do once it is inside the wound?
choices: it opens into thirty barbs that fill every joint and limb
it bursts into a cold blue flame
it splits the enemy's shadow from his body
it calls its twin spear across the battlefield to strike
rungs.answer: it opens into thirty barbs that fill every joint and limb
rungs.context: The medieval text says the spear enters as a single wound but opens into thirty barbs inside the flesh, filling every limb and joint. Wikipedia: Gae Bulg.

rungs.stem: Once the Gae Bolg has opened inside a body, the barbs make ordinary extraction impossible. Any warrior who tries to pull the spear back out through the entry wound only hooks the barbs deeper. In the Tain Bo Cuailnge, how is the Gae Bolg actually retrieved from the corpse?
choices: the flesh has to be cut open around it
it dissolves out of the wound after a day
the wielder whistles it back through the air
it must be pulled by two horses at once
rungs.answer: the flesh has to be cut open around it
rungs.context: In the Tain, Cu Chulainn's charioteer has to come forward after the killing of Ferdiad and cut the body open to take the Gae Bolg back -- the extraction kills the enemy a second time. Wikipedia: Gae Bulg.

rungs.stem: During the great cattle-raid of Cooley, Queen Medb of Connacht wants Cu Chulainn dead, but she cannot beat him with an ordinary champion. So she uses bribes, shame, and her daughter Findabair to ply an Irish champion with drink and force him to fight Cu Chulainn at the ford. Which warrior does Medb push into the ford?
choices: Ferdiad
Conall Cernach
Fergus mac Roich
Bricriu of the Poison Tongue
rungs.context: Ferdiad was Cu Chulainn's foster-brother -- they had trained together under Scathach and were equal in every feat but two. Wikipedia: Ferdiad.

rungs.stem: Ferdiad and Cu Chulainn had studied under the same master on the Isle of Shadow, and Scathach drilled them identically -- with two exceptions. Ferdiad had one advantage over Cu Chulainn: his skin could not be pierced by ordinary weapons. Cu Chulainn had the other, which was the secret Scathach's foster-house kept between them. What was Cu Chulainn's exclusive advantage?
choices: he alone had learned the Gae Bolg feat
he alone could see through Scathach's shape-shifting
he alone could ride the Grey of Macha under saddle
he alone knew the true name of the Morrigan
rungs.answer: he alone had learned the Gae Bolg feat
rungs.context: The Tain says the two foster-brothers were equal in all martial feats save that Ferdiad had impenetrable horn-skin and Cu Chulainn alone knew the Gae Bolg. Wikipedia: Ferdiad, Gae Bulg.

rungs.stem: On the last day of the ford-duel, Ferdiad has beaten every ordinary weapon Cu Chulainn has and Cu Chulainn is losing. He calls out to his charioteer for the one weapon he has been holding back. In the water of the ford, standing mid-current, who is the charioteer that floats the Gae Bolg down the stream to him?
choices: Loeg mac Riangabra
Conall Cernach
Fergus mac Roich
Sualtam mac Roich
rungs.context: Loeg is Cu Chulainn's lifelong charioteer; he floats the Gae Bolg down the current in the ford and later has to cut Ferdiad open to take the spear back out. Wikipedia: Gae Bulg.

rungs.stem: The moment the fight at the ford ends with the Gae Bolg in Ferdiad's belly, Cu Chulainn does something no ordinary champion of Medb's would do to a fallen enemy. He wades to Ferdiad, drags him out of the water, and carries him. What does Cu Chulainn do with Ferdiad's body immediately after the kill?
choices: he lifts it across the ford so no Connacht man can spoil it
he burns it on a raft launched down the current
he hangs it in a nearby oak as a warning to Medb
he sends it back to Medb's camp on his own chariot
rungs.answer: he lifts it across the ford so no Connacht man can spoil it
rungs.context: Cu Chulainn carries Ferdiad to the north bank -- the Ulster side -- and delivers a long formal lament for his foster-brother over the body. Wikipedia: Ferdiad.

rungs.stem: Standing over the body he has just killed with the Gae Bolg, Cu Chulainn breaks into a long formal lament for the foster-brother Medb's war has forced him to destroy. In the Tain, the first line of his lament is 'Ah, Ferdiad, betrayed to death. / Our last meeting, oh, how sad!' What is the third line of that opening?
choices: 'Thou to die -- I to remain.'
'The queen has taken thy honour.'
'The gods have set us at swords.'
'Alba weeps for her two sons.'
rungs.context: The lament turns the whole ford-episode from a victory into a wound -- Cu Chulainn is broken by having killed the brother Scathach's fosterage bound to him. Wikipedia: Ferdiad.

rungs.stem: The 'bolg' element in the spear's name has never been settled by Old Irish scholarship. The medieval glossators offer at least three competing readings that keep resurfacing in modern editions of the Tain. Which reading is NOT one of the traditional Old Irish glosses for 'bolg' in 'Gae Bolg'?
choices: 'sea-monster' (the beast of Coinchend)
'bag' (a bag-full of barbs)
'notch' or 'gap' in the metal
'belly' (the belly-spear)
rungs.context: 'Bag', 'notch', and 'belly' are the recurring medieval glosses; Eric Hamp reconstructs Proto-Celtic for 'spear of mortal pain'. The sea-monster-bone origin is a modern addition by Lady Gregory in 1902, not a medieval gloss. Wikipedia: Gae Bulg.

rungs.stem: No other hero in the Irish literature -- not Fionn mac Cumhaill with the Fianna, not Conall Cernach, not Lugh Lamhfhada with the spear of the Tuatha De Danann -- carries a weapon that works the way the Gae Bolg works. What single fact about the Gae Bolg is unique to Cu Chulainn's spear in the whole surviving Irish corpus?
choices: its foot-cast-from-water method of use
its power to kill kings and no others
its habit of returning to the caster's hand
its refusal to strike a wielder of its own kind
rungs.context: Lugh's spear (Areadbhar / Sleg) and Fionn's spear (Birgha) are famous but neither is cast from the toes in the water of a ford -- the Gae Bolg's method is one-of-a-kind in the medieval Irish sources. Wikipedia: Gae Bulg.
